questions.question: llama3.2 was trained on 131,072 tokens of context. You send a 4,000-token prompt with num_ctx 2048. What happens?
options: The model reads all 4,000 tokens anyway
About half the prompt is silently dropped
questions.explanation: num_ctx is the window Ollama actually allocates. Tokens beyond it are dropped with no error; only prompt_eval_count reveals it.

questions.question: Which field tells you whether a local model can call tools?
questions.explanation: capabilities lists what the model supports: completion, tools, embedding, vision, and so on.

questions.question: The first call takes 4.4s and the second takes 0.1s to start. Why?
options: The first call loaded the weights into memory (cold start); afterwards the model stays loaded for keep_alive
questions.explanation: load_duration shows the cold start. keep_alive (default 5m) controls how long the model stays warm.

questions.question: How do you make a local model return the same output on repeated runs?
options: Set temperature to 0 and fix a seed
questions.explanation: Greedy decoding (temperature 0) plus a fixed seed makes output repeatable, which you need for tests.

questions.question: "Characters ÷ 4" estimated 5,307 tokens, but Ollama counted 4,033. What's the right takeaway?
options: Use the rule of thumb for rough budgeting only; enforce limits with the tokenizer's real count (prompt_eval_count)
Token counts don't matter for local models
questions.explanation: Token ratios vary by tokenizer and text. Estimates are fine for planning; real counts decide truncation.

questions.question: Why do this course's agent lessons use /v1/chat/completions instead of Ollama's native /api/chat?
options: The OpenAI-compatible API is portable: the same code runs on Ollama, OpenAI, vLLM and others
questions.explanation: Portability. The native API is still the right tool for metadata, timings and load control, as this lesson shows.
